subject: Co-distribution proposal: SDK + model artifact escrow
messages:
From: Alex Grey <alex@openfoundry.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Co-distribution proposal: SDK + model artifact escrow

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking a minute to connect at the Summit last week — really enjoyed the runtime deep-dive. OpenFoundry is interested in a co-distribution partnership with Redwood where we bundle our lightweight inference SDK (edge+cloud) with selected open model artifacts. Our ask is two-fold:

- A vendor co-distribution agreement that lets us list the combined package in both marketplaces (OpenFoundry + Redwood ecosystem).
- An escrow mechanism for model weights and a short-form license that clarifies: distribution rights, attribution, and allowed commercial uses of the weights when redistributed through your channels.

High-level proposal:
- Revenue split: 70/30 in favor of OpenFoundry for first 12 months, then revisit based on install base.
- Escrow: third-party escrow (neutral custodian) holding canonical weights + provenance manifest; Redwood would have a signed, time-limited retrieval right for disaster recovery/fallback routing.
- SDK: OpenFoundry provides a permissive integration SDK and sample artifacts (we can share a 5MB zip).

Would love to set up a 30–45 minute call this week with your partnerships lead and legal/ops to walk through a pragmatic term sheet. I copied partnership@openfoundry (legal loop below).

Attachments: integration-sdk-sample.zip (small demo), one-pager.

Best,
Alex Grey
Head of Ecosystem Partnerships
OpenFoundry, Inc.
alex@openfoundry.ai
123-555-0191
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grey <alex@openfoundry.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-distribution proposal: SDK + model artifact escrow

Alex — great to hear from you and glad the Summit convo was useful. High level this sounds promising and aligned with how we think about publisher partnerships for model packaging.

Quick notes before a call:
- Partnership model: we usually propose a platform listing fee + revenue share; can be structured as a revenue split with a minimum guarantee for Redwood for first 6 months. Sergio, can you pull comparable splits from the 3 recent ISV deals?
- Escrow: we need clarity on retrieval triggers and who pays the escrow custodian fees. Our legal team will want a clause preventing escrow retrieval for unilateral redistribution (i.e., retrieval only for disaster recovery or compliance reasons).
- SDK: the sample looks compact — engineering would like to validate startup perf characteristics (latency, memory) before committing. Camila, can your team run a quick bake on a p3-small equivalent?

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync with Legal + Partnerships + Eng this Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda. Please attach the one-pager and the sample zip to the calendar invite for eng to pre-read.

Thanks — looking forward.

Vanessa Ortiz
Dir, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-distribution proposal: SDK + model artifact escrow

Vanessa / Sergio — putting down a few redline-first-pass items from PM/partnerships + ops perspective so we don’t go into the call blind. I attached a short term-sheet template for this type of arrangement (redwood-opengarden-term-sheet.docx).

Key points we should get clarity on during the call:
- Weights access model: distribution vs. mirrored cache. If OpenFoundry intends to allow redistribution of the weights via third parties we need explicit attribution rules and a revocation mechanism.
- Escrow retrieval triggers: proposed allowed triggers: (a) OpenFoundry insolvency, (b) breach of agreements resulting in takedown, (c) court order. Disallowed trigger: business convenience.
- Custodian & fees: prefer neutral custodian; propose each party pays 50% for the setup and OpenFoundry covers ongoing custody fees for first year unless metrics indicate heavy retrieval.
- QA & signature: we need a sample artifact and a small benchmark. Eng contact: rohan.mehta@redwood.com (please include him for perf validation).

Attachments: redwood-opengarden-term-sheet.docx (term-sheet stub).

Short agenda for Thu 10:00 PT:
1) Introductions + objectives (5m)
2) Escrow model and retrieval triggers (10m)
3) Revenue mechanics & marketplace listing (10m)
4) Technical validation plan and timelines (5m)

If legal wants to join the call feel free — otherwise we’ll capture notes and circulate a redline.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
Sr. Manager, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
From: Alex Grey <alex@openfoundry.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal (OpenFoundry) <legal@openfoundry.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-distribution proposal: SDK + model artifact escrow

Vanessa / Camila / Sergio — thanks for the quick review and the thoughtful questions. Thursday 10:00 PT works for us.

Couple of clarifications ahead of the call:
- Revenue: the 70/30 was an opening number — flexible. We can accept a minimum guarantee structure instead of a pure split if that simplifies approvals.
- Escrow: we’re fine with explicit retrieval triggers as proposed; OpenFoundry proposes Escrow Custodian "NeutralVault" (we can share contact). Can Redwood legal share a short custody SLA we require from them?
- Fees: happy to cover custodian setup + first-year maintenance.

I uploaded the SOW draft and a signed company letter for procurement: https://app.docusign.com/some-docusign-id/OPF-4721. I’m also attaching OpenFoundry_SOW_v1.pdf for your review (see attachment).

Looking forward to the call — I’ll send a calendar invite and include the DocuSign link for initial signature on the non-binding term-sheet.

Best,
Alex
Head of Ecosystem Partnerships
OpenFoundry, Inc.
